new_description: Duranium alloy plate, the standard hull armour of Starfleet starships. Plain, dependable, and repairable at any dock in the Federation. Gives almost no protection against fire; it is there to soak up damage. Of the Starfleet ship plates of its size, it is the cheapest to build and the easiest to repair, but the most fragile.

Transparent aluminium, the strong clear material of Starfleet viewports and cargo bay walls, laminated in layers and rolled opaque for use as hull plate. Its aluminium oxynitride matrix is aligned at the molecular level, so it is far stronger than it looks. Some protection against explosions. Of the Starfleet ship plates of its size, it is the lightest and the easiest to repair, but the weakest against beams.

A ceramic layer bonded to a duranium backing. The ceramic is seeded with a fractal lattice that shatters on impact and spreads the shock across the whole plate, so the backing is never loaded at a single point. Some protection against kinetic rounds and explosions. Of the Starfleet ship plates of its size, it is the weakest against beams.

Tritanium alloy, the hull and bulkhead metal of Galaxy- and Intrepid-class starships, laid in layers. Tritanium in its pure form is 21.4 times as hard as diamond. Good protection against explosions, some protection against kinetic rounds. Of the Starfleet ship plates of its size, it is the weakest against beams.

A crystalline laminate grown in the fabrication bays of the Utopia Planitia yards above Mars, with its atoms aligned along the line of the hull stress. The lattice vibrates at a resonant frequency, so a hit is spread through the crystal before it can crack. Good protection against explosions, some protection against kinetic rounds. Of the Starfleet ship plates of its size, it is the best protected against kinetic rounds and the best protected against explosions, but the costliest to build.

Ablative armour, as fitted to the USS Defiant: layers that burn away under fire and leave the hull beneath whole. Some protection against kinetic rounds, beams, energy fire and explosions. Of the Starfleet ship plates of its size, it is the toughest and the best protected against beams, but the heaviest.

Ablative plating for a starbase ring, replaced in sections once it has taken a beating. Strong protection against kinetic rounds, beams, energy fire and explosions, good protection against plasma. Of the Starfleet orbital plates of its size, it is the toughest and the best protected against beams, but the heaviest.

Plate grown on a bio-neural substrate, a living gel that senses damage and lays down new material at the edge of a breach. The substrate is tuned to the ship's own power grid, and the plate knits itself whole between engagements. Strong protection against every kind of fire. Of the Starfleet orbital plates of its size, it is the lightest.

A crystal lattice seeded on a bio-neural scaffold, which seals hairline cracks as they open. A trickle of power through the scaffold keeps the crystal growing back to its original pattern. Strong protection against every kind of fire. Of the Starfleet orbital plates of its size, it is the lightest and the best protected against plasma, but the costliest to build.

Polarised plating, a current run through the hull to stiffen it against impact. It was in use before shields, and still guards the rings of starbases. Some protection against kinetic rounds and explosions. Of the Starfleet orbital plates of its size, it is the cheapest to build and the easiest to repair, but the most fragile.
